study type: Secondary analysis of a cross-sectional survey
cohort: 205,648 singleton live births at 344 facilities in 23 low- and middle-income countries (LMICs)
finding: An outcome-based analysis of birth weight and early neonatal mortality in 23 LMICs suggests that a birth weight below 2200 g may be a more appropriate threshold for low birth weight in these settings, with potential regional variations.
country: 23 low- and middle-income countries (LMICs) in Africa, Asia, and Latin America
